pull.title: wallet, migration: Contain all legacy wallet and migration related things in its own subdirectory, namespace, and classes
pull.body:
Originally, legacy wallet migration was built upon the foundation of being able to load legacy wallets. Now that we no longer support loading legacy wallets, there is no reason to keep any of the legacy wallet loading and migration code in the main wallet objects. Having this co-mingling of never-to-be-changed legacy wallet code and new descriptor wallet code makes it difficult to implement new things into the wallet.

This PR fully separates out all of the legacy wallet related things into a subdirectory `wallet/legacy`, with everything in that directory under a `wallet::legacy_migration` namespace so as to prevent accidental usage outside of legacy wallets. This includes a little bit of duplication with current loading code, but not that much, and we are able to both remove unrelated descriptor wallet loading from the legacy wallet loading, and unrelated legacy wallet loading from normal descriptor wallet loading.

`LegacyWallet` is introduced as a subclass of `CWallet` which contains all of the relevant legacy wallet and migration functions so that `CWallet` cannot accidentally use some legacy wallet function. Additionally, `LegacyDataSPKM` is moved into a new file and this new namespace so that it cannot be used outside of migration.

Lastly, `ReorderTransactions` is a legacy wallet only function that is also moved into `LegacyWallet`.

Builds upon #34909, and depends on #36823 for removing some functions that were previously used by migration.

events.message:
wallet: migration, unify watchonly and solvables wallets creation

No need to repeat the exact same code twice.
This will let us introduce new safety checks and improve error
handling for both wallets without the risk of forgetting to
update one of them.

wallet: migration, handle exceptions during wallet creation

If creating the watch-only or solvables wallet throws, the migration is
now rolled back like other migration failures: the partially created
wallets are deleted and the original wallet is restored from the backup.

Previously the exception skipped this cleanup, so the user had to restore
the backup and delete the partially created wallets manually.

wallet: migration, restore backup if an exception is thrown

If MigrateToSQLite or DoMigration throws, the exception previously skipped the
failure handling at the end of MigrateLegacyToDescriptor. The RPC returned the
exception message, and the user was left with a partially migrated wallet and
had to restore the .legacy.bak backup and delete the new wallet files manually.

Catch these exceptions so the failed migration is cleaned up and the original
wallet is restored from the backup automatically, the same way as when
DoMigration returns an error.

wallet: fail migration gracefully on non-writable wallets

Currently, migrating a wallet whose database directory or file
is not writable throws a filesystem exception. Migration
then tries to restore the backup, which also throws again and
the user ends up seeing the raw exception.

Return a regular migration error instead, before the wallet is
modified. The error describes the problem better, and suggests
adjusting the permissions when that is the cause. The wallet
stays as it was, so the migration can be retried once the
problem is fixed without any manual intervention.

wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQLite

Write the migrated records with RunWithinTxn so failures to begin,
write or commit the transaction are handled in one place. A later
commit uses this to return an error instead of asserting.

This is a refactoring except on failure paths that still end in
assert(false): the new database is now closed and deleted when the
transaction can't be started or committed, not only when a write
fails, and the failure is properly logged.

wallet: migration, add MigrationFilePrefix() helper

Move the code that derives the backup file name prefix into a
helper, so the next commit can reuse it to name the temporary
database migration will build, leaving the original database
untouched until the new one has all the records.

The helpers are moved above MigrateToSQLite(), which will call it.

No behavior change.

wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures

Currently, MigrateToSQLite loads all BDB records into memory,
deletes the original database, creates the sqlite db in its
place, and writes the records to it. If anything fails after the
delete, the wallet is left partly in sqlite format with legacy
records, and the user has to restore the backup manually.

Instead, build the sqlite db in a temporary directory next to the
original db file, and once all records are written, rename it into
place. For wallet directories, the rename atomically replaces the
original wallet.dat, so any earlier failure leaves the original
untouched. A plain file wallet becomes a wallet directory, which
can't replace the file atomically, so the original file is erased
just before the move.

Before the move, check that no other files of the db, such as a
leftover journal, are at the destination, and fail if one is.
SQLite would otherwise roll a leftover journal back into the new
db when opening it, corrupting it.

Failures once the original db may have been erased or replaced
throw, so the migration restores the backup.
test: migrate wallet located on a different filesystem

test: migrate a wallet with a leftover journal at its location

Covers the leftover file removal added in "wallet: migration, make
sqlite creation robust against failures". Without it, SQLite rolls
the stale journal back into the migrated db once it is moved into
place, writing pages of an unrelated database into it.

wallet: Skip copy of legacy wallet records rather than erasing

Instead of erasing legacy wallet records and tx records from the
migrated database, skip copying these records in the first place.
wallet: Remove unused RemoveTxs and EraseTx
wallet, walletdb: Remove unused DeleteRecordsWithDB and EraseRecords

walletdb: Make HasLegacyRecords static

HasLegacyRecords is only used by LoadLegacyWalletRecords to check
whether a descriptor wallet has any legacy wallet records. This does not
require a CWallet, and is no longer called by anything outside of
walletdb.cpp.
wallet, migration: Move migration specific things to legacy subdir

wallet, migration: Put all migration related code into a namespace

Put all legacy wallet migration related code into a custom namespace to
clearly delineate which functions are migration and which are not, and
to prevent accidentally calling into migration functions from outside of
migration.

wallet, migration: Use a slimmed down wallet loading function

Instead of calling CWallet::LoadExisting, use a custom loading function
for migration only that does fewer things. This will be used in later
commits to implement a custom, migration specific, loading flow.
wallet, migration: Move legacy wallet loading code to migration module

wallet, migration: Add a LegacyWallet subclass of CWallet

LegacyWallet owns all of the wallet migration functions so that they do
not need to live in CWallet anymore.
wallet, migration: Move LegacyDataSPKM to its own file within migration

wallet, migration: Move ReorderTransactions to LegacyWallet

Reordering transactions is something that only legacy wallets will need
to do. All newly created descriptor wallets will have transactions with
order information. Migrated descriptor wallets will have computed the
order information during migration, and the updated tx records are
written to the new wallet, so always contain the order information.

wallet, migration: Remove unnecessary writes

When migrating a legacy wallet, there is no need to try to write
anything back into the legacy wallet, it won't work anyways.
wallet, migration: Move MigrationData to migration module
